{"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied with dominoes so nobody had to stop building. I made two full 40-domino runs to the boxes for the shared bin, at 0:45 and 1:45, early enough that the builders never ran dry. I also built the lower tail myself, tracing stroke 4 from the bottom line near the bump out to its end. It came out dark and connected, and it finishes the fish's tail. At the push, about 88 of the 93 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I chose large batches because a 40-domino trip costs 60 seconds, which is much cheaper per domino than small trips. I laid the lower tail in several short bursts and reported progress accurately: ten of fourteen down, then done. I stayed clear of the nose once the team agreed to leave it alone, which avoided bumps in that area.

Collaboration: I took on the lower tail when Priya asked, and I confirmed the assignments with Maya. I gave status updates so the others could plan around me, and I kept spare dominoes ready for patches. I respected the hands-off agreement on the nose.

Leadership: I led on supply. I anticipated what the table needed, acted without being asked twice, and kept my commitments on time. I also helped keep the group focused on the agreed plan in the final minutes.

Overall, I believe the supply work and the lower tail were important parts of getting a complete, recognizable fish that fell almost entirely from the start. I'd put my share at about 30 percent. Priya's sketch and the top line, Maya's bottom line, and Tom's upper tail and nose repair were also essential.", "my_share_percent": 30}
